name: Everygen.ai
subcategory: AI image and video generation for marketing assets
tagline: An AI studio for generating marketing images, avatars and short video clips from prompts and reference uploads.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Products like this are mostly a good UI, a preset library and a credit meter wrapped around hosted image and video models that someone else trains. An agent can rebuild the wrapper in a weekend: upload a reference, pick a preset, fan out a few variants, keep a local gallery. What it cannot rebuild is the model access, so you are swapping one subscription for a per-generation bill at fal.ai or Replicate, plus your own prompt tuning. If you generate a lot, that trade usually favours the DIY build; if you generate occasionally and want presets that already look right, it does not. Treat the DIY version as a personal generation console, not a studio.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you upload reference images, pick a saved preset prompt, fan out several variants through a hosted model API, and keep every output in a searchable local gallery.
requirements: An API key for a hosted model provider (fal.ai, Replicate or similar)
A credit card, since generation is billed per run
Patience for prompt and preset tuning, which is most of the actual work
whatYouLose: The curated preset library that makes outputs look intentional instead of generic
Whatever model routing and post-processing they do behind the scenes
Predictable flat pricing instead of a metered API bill that scales with your enthusiasm
Fast iteration on new model releases; you now maintain the integrations
Any team sharing, brand kits or asset approval flow
moatNotes: The defensible bit is preset taste and model plumbing, not the generation itself. If they fine-tune their own models the moat is real; if they resell someone else's API it is thin.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because raw model APIs produce mush and presets produce results. Most buyers here are marketers and solo founders who want a product shot or a talking-head clip in four clicks, not a prompt engineering hobby, and they are happy to pay a margin on top of inference to skip the part where you learn which sampler and aspect ratio combination stops the hands from melting. The subscription also caps the bill, which matters psychologically more than it should.
notes: The UI is a weekend; the taste in the preset library is the product.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI generation console called "Everygen Lite". Single user, no accounts, no telemetry, runs on my machine.

Stack, non negotiable: Next.js with the App Router and TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, SQLite via better-sqlite3 for metadata, generated files written to ./storage on disk. No Docker, no auth, no cloud database.

Model access: use fal.ai as the single generation provider through its REST API. Put FAL_KEY in .env.local and read it server side only. Define the provider behind one module at lib/providers/fal.ts exposing generateImage(params) and generateVideo(params) so a second provider could be added later. Do not add a second provider now.

Features that are in scope:
1. Presets. A JSON file at data/presets.json defining named presets: label, model id, prompt template with {{subject}} and {{style}} placeholders, negative prompt, aspect ratio, default variant count. Ship six starter presets: product on seamless backdrop, lifestyle product shot, headshot cleanup, social square graphic, cinematic 5 second clip, logo mark exploration.
2. A generate page: pick a preset, fill the template variables, optionally upload up to three reference images, choose variant count 1 to 4, submit.
3. Queue and status. Store each run as a job row with status queued, running, done, failed, provider request id, cost estimate if the API returns one, and the fully resolved prompt. Poll job status server side; the UI refreshes via a simple interval fetch.
4. Gallery. Grid of all outputs with the resolved prompt, preset name, created date, and buttons to download, delete, or re-run with the same inputs. Full text search over prompts. Filter by preset.
5. Spend log. A page summing per-run cost estimates by day and month so I can see the API bill before the API bill sees me.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, team sharing, brand kits, billing, in-browser image editing, video timeline editing, model training or fine tuning, background job servers like Redis.

Deliverables: working app, README with setup steps, a .env.example listing FAL_KEY, a seed script that inserts the starter presets, and clear inline comments where a second provider would plug in. Handle API failures by marking the job failed and showing the provider error text verbatim rather than swallowing it.
